title: Cartesian generator charts and finiteness of the saturation comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $P$ a finitely generated integral monoid with group completion $G$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $\alpha:P\to A$ a chart, and $E\subset P$ finite nonempty. Put $Q_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle\subset G$ and $Q_e^s=\{q\in G:\exists n>0,\ nq\in Q_e\}$. For $\epsilon=0,s$, suppose $X^\epsilon$ is a log scheme over $(\operatorname{Spec}A,P)$ covered by open charts
$$X_e^0=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e]),\qquad X_e^s=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^s]),$$
with the associated monoid log structures [def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Assume their pairwise intersections and gluing isomorphisms are the common monomial localizations $D(z^{f-e})\simeq D(z^{e-f})$, and that the log ideal generated by $E$ is generated by $e$ on each $e$-chart. The inclusions $Q_e\subseteq Q_e^s$ induce compatible chart maps and a log morphism $s:X^s\to X^0$ over $(\operatorname{Spec}A,P)$. In either $X^\epsilon$, the $e$-chart is exactly the locus where $e$ generates the pulled-back log ideal. One has $s^{-1}(X_e^0)=X_e^s$, and the square of these open immersions and the corresponding chart map is Cartesian on underlying schemes. For any finite $F_e\subset Q_e^s$ with $Q_e^s=\bigcup_{f\in F_e}(f+Q_e)$, the $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e]$-module $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^s]$ is generated by $1\otimes z^f$ for $f\in F_e$. Such finite $F_e$ exist, and $s$ is finite: the inverse image of every affine open in $X^0$ is affine with a finite coordinate algebra. These maps, Cartesian chart squares and finiteness commute with strict etale base change of the base chart.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101; 3.2.9, finiteness sentence only, printed p. 104; 3.3.9, printed p. 108: saturation chart comparison and its finite affine chart preimages.

proof.text: Each $Q_e$ is generated by generators of $P$ and the finite list $h-e$. It is integral as a submonoid of $G$, and $Q_e^{\mathrm{gp}}=G$: every $g\in G$ is $p-p\prime$ with $p,p\prime\in P\subseteq Q_e$, and equality of two such differences is exactly the group-completion relation, since $Q_e$ is cancellative. Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation] to $Q_e$ in this group completion. It gives finite $F_e\subset Q_e^s$ with $Q_e^s=\bigcup_{f\in F_e}(f+Q_e)$, and says $Q_e^s$ is finitely generated and saturated. Thus the chart log schemes are fine, and the saturated chart log schemes are fs.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101; 3.2.9, finiteness sentence of proof, printed p. 104.

proof.text: On $X_e^s$ the ideal is generated by $e$. Apply the fine lifting clause of [lem-trf-log-ideal-chart-lifting-criterion] with $T=X_e^s$ to obtain the unique map $s_e:X_e^s\to X_e^0$. Its chart homomorphism is $Q_e\hookrightarrow Q_e^s$, so its ring map is $a\otimes z^q\mapsto a\otimes z^q$. On the $e,f$ overlap both $e$ and $f$ generate. The overlap clause of that same node says these lifts factor through the common principal opens and agree there, including their log maps. Hence the $s_e$ glue to $s:X^s\to X^0$ over the base: on any open, define the structure-sheaf and log-sheaf maps by their agreeing restrictions to these charts; uniqueness is the sheaf condition.

Fix $\epsilon$ and a geometric point of $X_f^\epsilon$ at which $e$ also generates. The simultaneous-generator clause of [lem-trf-log-ideal-chart-lifting-criterion] says the difference $e-f$ is a unit in the log stalk. Its structural image $1\otimes z^{e-f}$ is therefore a unit in the local ring, so the point lies in $D(1\otimes z^{e-f})=X_f^\epsilon\cap X_e^\epsilon$ by the assumed overlaps. Conversely $e$ generates everywhere on $X_e^\epsilon$ by hypothesis. Since the $f$-charts cover, this proves the generator-locus assertion, also at ordinary points by passage to geometric points.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19 and 3.3.8--3.3.9: ideal-fraction overlaps and distinguished generators.

proof.text: On $X_f^s$ the map $s$ is $s_f$ with image in $X_f^0$. Its inverse image of $X_e^0\cap X_f^0=D(1\otimes z^{e-f})$ is $D(1\otimes z^{e-f})\subset X_f^s$, since the ring map fixes that monomial. The overlap assumption identifies this open with $X_e^s\cap X_f^s$. Taking the union over $f$ proves $s^{-1}(X_e^0)=X_e^s$ as open subschemes, and the restriction is $s_e$. This is the Cartesian square: a map to $X^s$ whose composite factors through $X_e^0$ factors uniquely through this inverse-image open, precisely the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, localization compatibility; 3.3.9, chart saturation comparison.

proof.text: Let any finite $F_e$ as in the statement be given, and write $B_e=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e]$, $C_e=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q_e^s]$. The tensor product is additively generated by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and every element of the monoid algebra is a finite sum of monomials. For $q\in Q_e^s$ choose $f\in F_e$, $p\in Q_e$ with $q=f+p$. Then $a\otimes z^q=(a\otimes z^p)(1\otimes z^f)$. Expanding a finite sum gives a $B_e$-linear combination of the claimed generators. This uses no injectivity of the map $B_e\to C_e$ and remains valid if a tensor chart ring is zero.

source.place: VIII 3.2.9, finite toric saturation map; explicit monomial spanning after tensor base change.

proof.text: For the finite $F_e$ from Step 1, Step 5 makes $C_e$ a finite $B_e$-module. The affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite] therefore makes $s_e:\operatorname{Spec}C_e\to\operatorname{Spec}B_e$ finite. Step 4 identifies it with the full inverse image over $X_e^0$, not merely a map from an affine source open. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] to the affine open cover $(X_e^0)_{e\in E}$ of $X^0$. It follows that $s$ is finite. In particular every affine open has affine inverse image and finite coordinate algebra, by the definition of a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01WI (lemma-finite-local), and Tag 01WH (definition-integral), in morphisms.tex, lines 11001 and 10957.

proof.text: Apply the arbitrary-ring-base-change clause of [lem-trf-log-ideal-affine-atlas-gluing] to $A\to A\prime$. It identifies the base-changed charts and exact overlaps, with their pulled-back log structures, with those formed using $A\prime$. The chart ring identifications send $a\prime\otimes(a\otimes z^q)$ to $a\prime a\otimes z^q$. In both orders the comparison sends $a\otimes z^q$ to the same monomial; its log map is the same inclusion $Q_e\subseteq Q_e^s$. Thus the comparisons agree on every chart and overlap and hence globally. The inverse-image opens in Step 4 base-change to the same principal opens, proving compatibility of the Cartesian squares. The same finite $F_e$ and the calculation in Step 5 prove finiteness after this base change. For a strict etale base change the log structure is the pulled-back one; working on its affine pieces gives exactly these identifications, which agree on overlaps. This proves every asserted compatibility.

source.place: VIII 3.3.5--3.3.9, printed pp. 107--108: strict chart base change and saturation comparison.
